chapters.title: SLA policies and business hours
intro: This chapter is for supervisors and administrators. It explains how SupportDesk measures service commitments, and how you set them up.
Supervisors use the **SLA** module to watch tickets at risk. Administrators also create policies, business calendars and holidays.

sections.title: What an SLA measures
intro: An SLA policy sets time targets for each ticket priority. The clock for each target is called a milestone.
Open **SLA** in the left rail. Its tabs are **Policies**, **Calendars & holidays** and **Live breaches**.

rows: Time until an agent first replies to the customer. This clock never pauses.
Time until an agent answers the customer's latest message.
Time until the ticket is resolved.

list: **At risk**: the milestone passed its warning point, for example 75% of the target.
**Paused**: the ticket is in a status that pauses SLA clocks, such as **Waiting on Customer**.

blocks.p: SupportDesk checks every running milestone every 30 seconds. Warnings and escalations fire from that check.

rows: Open the SLA module and read policies and calendars
Create, change, reorder or delete policies
Create or change business calendars and holidays

blocks.note: Without the right permission, the forms show the settings but you cannot change them.

sections.title: How a policy is chosen
sections.intro: Each ticket gets exactly one SLA policy. SupportDesk picks it in this order:

list: First: the policy of the ticket's active contract.
Next: the first active policy, in evaluation order, whose conditions match the ticket.

blocks.p: The business calendar comes from the contract's support hours first. Next come the policy's calendar and the department's calendar. With none of these, the clock runs 24x7.
When you change a policy or the evaluation order, open tickets are checked again. Time already elapsed is kept.

blocks.note: The department's **Default SLA policy** field does not take part in this choice in this release.

sections.title: The Policies tab
sections.intro: Open **SLA** > **Policies** to see every policy in evaluation order.

blocks.caption: The **Policies** tab with a Platinum policy and the default Standard SLA.
blocks.alt: Policies tab with numbered tabs, New policy button, explanation, table header and order buttons

callouts: The SLA tabs.
**New policy** opens an empty policy.
A reminder of how a policy is chosen.
Columns: order number, policy name and version, calendar, conditions, targets, escalations, running milestones and last update.
The arrows move a policy up or down the evaluation order.

blocks.p: **Default** marks the fallback policy. It always comes last and shows **Fallback** in the **Conditions** column. **Inactive** marks a policy that is switched off.

sections.title: Change the evaluation order
sections.intro: Put specific policies above general ones. The first matching policy wins.
steps: Open **SLA** > **Policies**.
Select the up or down arrow on a policy row. Repeat until the order is right.
Select **Save order**. To undo your moves, select **Discard**.
sections.result: A message says "Evaluation order saved". Open tickets are checked again.

sections.title: The policy editor
sections.intro: Select a policy to open it. The editor has five cards from top to bottom.

blocks.caption: The policy editor for the Platinum 24x7 policy.
blocks.alt: Policy editor with numbered Delete and Save policy buttons, and Policy, Applies to, Targets per priority, Escalation levels and Simulate cards

callouts: **Delete** and **Save policy**. The header also shows the version and how many tickets run on the policy.
**Policy**: name, status, business calendar and pause statuses.
**Applies to**: the conditions a ticket must meet. The default policy has no conditions.
**Targets per priority**: the time targets and the warning point.
**Escalation levels**: what happens before or after a breach.
**Simulate against a ticket**: test the form on a real ticket before you save.

sections.title: Create an SLA policy
steps: Open **SLA** > **Policies** and select **New policy**.

steps.text: In the **Policy** card, enter the **Name** and a **Description**.
steps.caption: The **Policy** card of the Platinum 24x7 policy.
steps.alt: Policy card with name, description, Active, Default policy, business calendar, pause statuses and contract hours option

steps: Choose the **Business calendar** and any extra **Pause statuses**.
If contracts set their own support hours, tick the contract option at the bottom of the card.

steps.text: In **Applies to**, select **Condition** and build the rule, such as **Customer tier** is `Platinum`.
steps.caption: The **Applies to** card with one condition on the customer tier.
steps.alt: Applies to card with All (AND) and Any (OR), a customer tier condition, and Condition and Group buttons

steps: Set the targets. See [Set targets per priority](#sla-targets).
Add escalation levels if you need them. See [Add escalation levels](#sla-escalations).
Select **Save policy**.
sections.result: A message says "SLA policy saved". The policy joins the list as version 1.

blocks.p: The contract option reads **Use the contract's support hours when the ticket is covered by a contract**.
Choose **All (AND)** when every condition must match, or **Any (OR)** when one is enough. **Group** adds a nested group. Groups can go three levels deep.
Conditions can use the ticket, customer, contact and contract. Examples are tier, contract, priority, department, product, category and channel.

blocks.tip: A policy without conditions matches every ticket. Put it near the bottom of the evaluation order.

sections.title: Set targets per priority
steps: In the policy editor, go to **Targets per priority**.
Tick each priority that the policy covers: **Critical**, **High**, **Medium** or **Low**.
For each priority, enter the **First response**, **Next response** and **Resolution** times.
Choose the unit for each time: **min**, **h** or **d**.
Tick **Business** to count only the calendar's working time.
In **Warn at**, enter the warning point as a percentage of the target.
Select **Save policy**.
sections.result: The policy uses the new targets. Saving creates a new version and recalculates open tickets.

blocks.caption: Targets for four priorities with 24x7 counting.
blocks.alt: Targets per priority table with first response, next response and resolution times, business hours boxes and warning percentages

blocks.note: Targets can range from 1 minute to 365 days. **Warn at** takes 1–99%. The default is 75%.

sections.title: Add escalation levels
sections.intro: An escalation level acts when a milestone gets close to a breach, or after it. A policy can have up to 10 levels.
steps: In the policy editor, go to **Escalation levels** and select **Add level**.
Choose the **Milestone** and enter the **Level** number.
In **When**, choose **At % of target** or **Minutes from breach**.
Enter the **Percent** or the **Minutes**.
Choose the **Action**.
For a reassign action, choose **Reassign to agent** or **…or to team**.
For a notify action, tick **Notify assignee** and **Notify supervisors**, and add people under **Also notify**.
Select **Save policy**.
sections.result: The level fires when the milestone reaches the point you set.

blocks.caption: Three escalation levels: a breach notice, a warning an hour before, and a reassignment.
blocks.alt: Escalation levels card with milestone, level, when, minutes, action, reassign and notify fields for three levels

rows: Fires at a share of the target. `80` fires before the breach. `150` fires after it.
Fires a number of minutes around the breach. A negative number fires before it.
Moves the ticket to the agent or team you choose.
Sends a notification and moves the ticket.

blocks.p: To delete a level, select **Remove** on it. Without levels, breaches show on the risk boards only.

sections.title: Simulate a policy against a ticket
sections.intro: Check which policy a ticket would get, and its due times, before you save. The simulation uses the unsaved form.
steps: Open the policy and make your changes.
In **Simulate against a ticket**, enter a **Ticket number**.
Select **Simulate**.
sections.result: The card shows the selected policy and the reason. It lists every policy as **Selected**, **Matches** or **Skipped**, and the new due times.

blocks.caption: The simulation for ticket #1010 selects Platinum 24x7.
blocks.alt: Simulate card with ticket 1010, the selected policy, the evaluated policies and a table of milestones with targets and due times

blocks.p: **Differs from the current SLA** means saving would change the ticket's policy. The **Current** column shows the due time the ticket has now.

sections.title: Deactivate or delete a policy
steps: Open the policy.
To switch it off, clear **Active**, then select **Save policy**.
To remove it, select **Delete**, then **Delete** in the confirmation.
sections.result: An inactive policy stays in the list but no longer matches tickets. A deleted policy disappears.

blocks.note: You cannot delete the default policy. You cannot delete a policy that tickets have used, or that a contract names. Deactivate those instead.

sections.title: Business calendars
intro: A business calendar sets the working hours and holidays in a time zone. SLA clocks with **Business** ticked count only this time.
Open **SLA** > **Calendars & holidays**. Departments, policies and contracts can each use a calendar.

blocks.caption: The **Calendars & holidays** tab with the default business hours calendar open.
blocks.alt: Calendars tab with numbered New calendar button, calendar list, edit form, weekly hours, Save calendar, holidays and business time preview

callouts: **New calendar**.
The calendars, with hours per week, time zone and holidays. **Default** and **Used** badges show how each is used.
The name, time zone, description, **Open 24x7** and **Default calendar** settings.
The weekly hours, with presets such as **Mon–Fri 09–18**.
**Save calendar**. Below it, **Used by** lists what uses the calendar.
**Holidays** for this calendar.
**Business time preview**.

sections.title: Create or edit a business calendar
steps: Open **SLA** > **Calendars & holidays**.
Select **New calendar**, or select a calendar in the list.
Enter the **Name** and choose the **Time zone**.
Turn on **Open 24x7 (no business hours)**, or set the weekly hours.
For weekly hours, select a preset, then adjust each day. Select **Split** to add a break.
Turn on **Default calendar** if this calendar should be the default.
Select **Save calendar**.
sections.result: A message says "Calendar saved". The list shows the new hours per week.

blocks.p: To delete a calendar, select it and select **Delete**. You cannot delete the default calendar, or a calendar that departments, policies or contracts use.

sections.title: Add a holiday
sections.intro: Holidays are whole local days that SLA business time skips.
steps: Open **SLA** > **Calendars & holidays** and select the calendar.
In **Holidays**, enter the **Date** and the **Name**.
Tick **Every year** for a holiday on the same date each year.
Select **Add**.
sections.result: The holiday appears in the table. **Repeats** shows **Every year** or **Once**.

blocks.caption: The **Holidays** card with five holidays.
blocks.alt: Holidays card with Import CSV, the add form and a table of dates, names and repeats

blocks.p: To remove a holiday, select the remove button on its row.

sections.title: Import holidays from a CSV file
sections.intro: Load a year of holidays at once from a spreadsheet.
steps: Open **SLA** > **Calendars & holidays** and select the calendar.

steps.caption: The **Import holidays** dialog with three sample lines.
steps.alt: Import holidays dialog with a CSV text box, Choose File button and Replace all existing holidays option

steps: Paste the lines into **CSV**. Or use the file button below the box to load a CSV file.
Turn on **Replace all existing holidays** only if the file is the full new list.
Select **Import**.
Read the result, then select **Done**.
sections.result: A message says how many holidays were added, updated and skipped. Up to 50 line errors are listed.

blocks.warning: **Replace all existing holidays** deletes the current holidays, even if every imported line fails.

rows: Blank lines, lines starting with `#`, and a first line starting with `date`.

sections.title: Check business time with the preview
sections.intro: See how much business time lies between two moments, and when a target would fall due. Nothing is saved.
steps: Open **SLA** > **Calendars & holidays** and select the calendar.
In **Business time preview**, enter **From** and **To**.
Optionally, enter **Add business minutes**, such as the target of a milestone.
Select **Calculate**.
sections.result: The card shows the business time against the total time, the holidays in range, and each working interval. With minutes added, it shows when the target falls due.

blocks.caption: The preview counts 20 hours of business time across four working days.
blocks.alt: Business time preview with from and to dates, 120 business minutes and the result with working intervals

sections.title: Live breaches
intro: Open **SLA** > **Live breaches** to see every running milestone that is at risk or breached. The soonest due come first.
Each ticket can appear more than once, once for each milestone.

blocks.caption: The **Live breaches** tab with 23 open breaches.
blocks.alt: Live breaches tab with numbered Refresh button, KPI tiles, state, milestone and department filters, and table header

callouts: **Refresh** reloads the list.
Tiles for **At risk**, **Breached (open)**, **Breached today**, **Due in the next hour** and **Paused**. Select **At risk** or **Breached (open)** to filter the list.
The state filter: **At risk and breached**, **At risk** or **Breached**.
The milestone filter.
The department filter.
Columns: ticket, milestone with priority and escalation level, due time, elapsed time against the target, owner, department and policy.

blocks.p: **L1** and **L2** show the escalation level a milestone reached. The **Elapsed** bar turns amber at 75% and red at 100% of the target.

blocks.tip: Select a ticket number to open the ticket. Select **Load more** at the bottom for older items.

troubleshooting.cause: Every workspace needs a fallback policy.
troubleshooting.fix: Make another policy the default first. Then delete the old one.

troubleshooting.problem: "Tickets have used this policy, so it is kept for reproducibility."
troubleshooting.cause: Past tickets refer to the policy.
troubleshooting.fix: Clear **Active** and save the policy instead of deleting it.

troubleshooting.cause: One or more contracts name this policy.
troubleshooting.fix: Change those contracts first, then delete the policy.

troubleshooting.problem: "Departments, SLA policies or contracts use this calendar."
troubleshooting.cause: You try to delete a calendar that is in use.
troubleshooting.fix: Check **Used by** under the calendar. Change those items first.

troubleshooting.cause: The default calendar is the fallback for new items.
troubleshooting.fix: Make another calendar the default first.

troubleshooting.problem: A ticket gets the wrong policy.
troubleshooting.cause: A policy higher in the evaluation order also matches, or a contract sets the policy.
troubleshooting.fix: Open a policy and use **Simulate against a ticket**. The list shows why each policy was selected or skipped.

troubleshooting.cause: **Business** is not ticked for that target, or the calendar is open 24x7.
troubleshooting.fix: Tick **Business** for the target and choose a calendar with weekly hours.

troubleshooting.problem: The policy form fields are greyed out.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask an administrator to change the policy, or to give you the permission.

faq.q: Does the first response clock pause when the ticket waits on the customer?
faq.a: No. The first response clock never pauses. Pause statuses stop only the next response and resolution clocks.

faq.q: What happens to open tickets when I change a policy?
faq.a: Saving creates a new version of the policy. Open tickets are recalculated, and time already elapsed is kept.

faq.q: Why does a ticket appear twice on Live breaches?
faq.a: The list shows milestones, not tickets. A ticket shows once for each milestone that is at risk or breached.

glossary.definition: Working hours and holidays in a time zone. SLA clocks with business hours count only this time.
An action, such as a notification or reassignment, that fires at a set point before or after an SLA breach.
The order in which SLA policies are checked. The first active policy whose conditions match a ticket wins.
One SLA clock on a ticket: first response, next response or resolution.
A ticket status during which SLA response and resolution clocks stop counting.
A milestone whose target time has passed before the agent met it.
A set of time targets per priority, with conditions and escalation levels, that applies to matching tickets.
